page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the E2 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. The single-core stress-ng score of 1103.39 and multi-core score of 1451.58 place it in the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth is limited, with uncached large-block read speeds at 11.77 GB/sec and write speeds at 10.27 GB/sec. Similarly, the Geekbench single-core score of 867.0 and multi-core score of 1025.0 reflect its entry-level processing capacity.

Given these performance metrics, the e2-standard-2 is best suited for lightweight, non-intensive workloads. These include basic web serving, where it achieves a static throughput of 1.45 GB/sec, small-scale database operations, and minor text or image processing tasks. While its raw compute and memory throughput are modest, the instance offers a cost-effective profile for development environments, staging servers, and simple utility services that do not require high-performance hardware.
description: The Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-2 is an entry-level, general-purpose virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture instance provides a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark results indicate modest performance, with a single-core Geekbench score of 867.0 and a multi-core score of 1025.0, placing its compute and memory bandwidth capabilities in the lower percentiles. Consequently, this instance is highly cost-efficient for lightweight applications rather than resource-intensive operations. It is best suited for basic web serving, development environments, small-scale database tasks, and low-throughput utility workloads.
